subject: Unexpected tail latency and increased 5xxs on Hemlock on‑prem — exec sync requested
messages:
From: Samira Rao <samira@hemlockhealth.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 3 Jun 2028 14:12:00 -0400
Subject: Sharp p99 spikes + 502s this morning on our on‑prem cluster

Jordan —

We started seeing a dramatic increase in tail latency and a small but growing number of 502s on our private cluster after the maintenance window this morning. p50 is fine (50–70ms) but p95 jumped to ~1.8s and p99 is hitting 4–6s for our clinical summarization endpoint. We also saw a cluster of 502s between 08:10–08:40 UTC (attached traces).

This is impacting the triage UI and a few automated workflows have missed SLAs; our CTO is now asking for an executive summary and an immediate mitigation plan. We applied the recommended quantization profile last week — can that be correlated?

Attached: hemlock_p99_spikes_20280603.png, hemlock_tail_traces_20280603.log

Can you confirm whether Redwood can roll us back to the previous runtime config or run a hotfix? We need an ETA and any steps we should take on our side (netstat, stack dumps, etc).

—Samira
Samira Rao
VP Product, Hemlock Health
samira@hemlockhealth.com
From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Samira Rao <samira@hemlockhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 3 Jun 2028 14:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sharp p99 spikes + 502s this morning on our on‑prem cluster

Thanks for the heads up, Samira — and sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as high priority.

Quick read: the attachment points to sustained p99 jumps that line up with a burst of long decode times; 502s appear correlated with queue overflow on a single node.

Immediate next steps (we'll own these):
- I am opening a triage war room with our Private SRE team now.
- We'll snapshot the customer’s runtime config and evaluate rolling back the quantization/engine change you mentioned.
- Please keep the logs coming; if you can, send the node IDs for the affected pods and any recent kubelet logs.

Marissa (AE) — looping you in for procurement/contract implications and for the exec thread. I will update within 30 minutes with an initial cause hypothesis.

On Mon Jun 4 08:10:12 2028 Samira wrote:
> Jordan —
>
> We started seeing a dramatic increase...

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Account Director, Redwood Inference
From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 3 Jun 2028 14:42:00 -0400
Subject: Hemlock on‑prem incident: triage notes + ask list

Team — quick internal summary and asks before we escalate to a CTO sync. (Internal only)

Summary:
- Customer: Hemlock Health (private deployment).
- Symptom: p95/p99 tail latency increase (p99 4–6s) and intermittent 502s tied to node queue overload.
- Recent change: recommended quantization profile applied 2028‑05‑28; also runtime kernel tweak during maintenance 06:00 UTC this morning.

Immediate actions (owners):
- Ops (SRE) — capture hot thread traces from affected nodes, gather decode time distribution, check KV cache hit/miss rate (owner: oncall-sre).
- Runtime Eng — evaluate whether the new kernel selection caused decoder stall under long sequences; if validated, prepare rollback patch for canary.
- Support (Marissa) — schedule CTO sync window and prepare customer-facing timeline and compensation guideline.

Proposed mitigations to propose to customer in CTO sync:
1) Canary rollback of quantization + restart of affected node set (fast path, low risk).
2) Short-term rate limit on long-sequence requests and auto-fallback to a lower‑throughput model variant.
3) Deep dive runbook (24h) with hourly updates.

I'll take point with SRE and Runtime Eng and will post the war‑room link. Laura — can you join the exec sync if Samira requests? Marissa — please prep a one‑pager for finance if we need a credit.

Jordan
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Samira Rao <samira@hemlockhealth.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 07:15:00 -0400
Subject: Hemlock — exec sync & remediation plan proposal

Samira —

I'm Laura Bennett, Head of Customer Success at Redwood. First, I'm very sorry for the impact this morning — thank you for surfacing the traces. We have mobilized SRE and Runtime Eng and want to propose an immediate, low‑risk path and a short remediation timeline: 

Proposed immediate plan (can be actioned within ~45 minutes after your OK):
- Canaries: rollback the quantization profile to your prior setting on 10% of nodes and monitor p99 for 30 minutes.
- Rate‑limit: apply a temporary safeguard that drops long sequences >4k tokens to a fallback model variant for 10 minutes if the canary shows improvement.
- Node restart: if canary stabilizes, schedule a rolling restart of the remaining affected nodes with staggered drain to avoid bulk queue collapse.

We will provide an exec summary and a remediation timeline in the next 60 minutes. Can we schedule a 30‑minute sync at 08:00 UTC to go through the plan? If that doesn't work, we'll do async updates every 30 minutes.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
From: Samira Rao <samira@hemlockhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: Diego Morales <diego.morales@hemlockhealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hemlock — exec sync & remediation plan proposal

Laura / Jordan — thanks for the quick mobilization and clear plan. 08:00 UTC works for our CTO and me. Please proceed with the 10% canary rollback and share the war room link. On our side we'll collect kubelet logs and isolate the affected node IDs; Diego will upload a short timeline to the Drive link you shared.

If the canary shows improvement, we'll greenlight rolling restarts. Appreciate the transparency and the suggested temporary fallback option — that should help keep our triage UI stable while you walk back the change.

—Samira
